label: PASS — AMR Surveillance, Accurate Parameters, Comprehensive Scope

generated_draft.background: The Antibiotic Resistance Laboratory Network (ARLN) coordinates state and regional public health laboratory capacity to detect and characterize novel and emerging antimicrobial resistance threats. Priority organisms include carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE), carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA), carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB), and Candida auris — an emerging multidrug-resistant fungal pathogen with significant nosocomial transmission risk. This cooperative agreement expands ARLN-participating state laboratory capacity for both phenotypic susceptibility testing and molecular resistance mechanism characterization using WGS.
generated_draft.funding_parameters: Total available funding: $3,600,000. Awards: 14–18. Range per laboratory: $100,000–$300,000. Period of performance: 24 months (October 1, 2021 – September 30, 2023). Federal sponsor: CDC / NCEZID / DHCPP. Cost sharing: not required.
generated_draft.eligibility: Public Health Labs member state laboratory with ARLN participation or readiness. CLIA high-complexity certification. Broth microdilution (BMD) susceptibility testing capability for CRE. CarbaNP or modified carbapenem inactivation method (mCIM) implementation. Partnership with state HAI program.
generated_draft.scope_of_work: 1. Achieve ARLN Reference Laboratory status (if not yet designated) within 12 months. Implement BMD for carbapenem MIC determination for CRE, CRPA, and CRAB per CLSI standards. 2. Implement Candida auris identification by MALDI-TOF and antifungal susceptibility testing (echinocandin and azole MICs) per CLSI M27. 3. Submit ≥95% of carbapenemase-producing isolates for WGS to CDC AR Lab Network within 5 business days. 4. Implement carbapenemase gene detection (KPC, NDM, VIM, OXA-48, IMP) by multiplex PCR or molecular beacon method per ARLN protocol.
generated_draft.reporting_requirements: Monthly ARLN sentinel data submissions to CDC NHSN. Quarterly C. auris surveillance reports. WGS submission timeliness reports quarterly. Outbreak cluster reports within 48 hours. Final report 90 days post-period of performance.
generated_draft.budget_requirements: BMD susceptibility testing reagents (TREK Sensititre or equivalent) allowable. MALDI-TOF library expansion for C. auris allowable. Carbapenemase PCR reagents and controls allowable. WGS library preparation consumables allowable. ARLN proficiency participation costs allowable.
generated_draft.evaluation_criteria: Current ARLN participation and capacity (20 points). CRE and CRPA testing plan (25 points). Candida auris surveillance approach (25 points). WGS and molecular characterization (20 points). Budget justification (10 points).
generated_draft.submission_instructions: Deadline: November 19, 2021, 5:00 PM Eastern Time. Submit via Public Health Labs Grants Portal. Required: Narrative (15 pages), Budget, ARLN designation letter or readiness documentation, current CRE testing SOP, HAI program partnership letter, mCIM validation documentation.

evaluator_notes: Comprehensive draft with all 8 sections. Parameters exactly match source. ARLN acronym expansion accurate (Antibiotic Resistance Laboratory Network). Candida auris, CRE, CRPA all correctly framed. CLSI standard references (M27 for antifungal) accurate. mCIM correctly named (modified carbapenem inactivation method). No prohibited language. Groundedness high — technical claims verifiable against ARLN program documentation context.
